# Appeal of Denial – Lower Back Disc Surgery (CPT 63030)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Morgan Foster
**Member ID:** W162894592
**Reference Number:** POC-F4C641ED8B-99591
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-23
**Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), State of Illinois
**Governing Policy:** Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114), https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

Dear Ambetter Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030). My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition, and I believe the records already in your possession meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## How My Records Meet the Plan's Criteria

Your policy states that discectomy is medically necessary when meeting all of the following:

> "discectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following:"

**1. Diagnosis of a herniated lumbar disc**

The plan's policy requires:

> "Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc;"

My MRI of the lumbar spine, performed 2026-06-26, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion, which is a herniated lumbar disc.

**2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging**

The plan's policy requires:

> "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

The same MRI documents severe right lateral recess stenosis with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is imaging-confirmed nerve root compression.

**3. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit**

The plan's policy recognizes this pathway:

> "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

My records document radicular pain extending into my right calf, in the distribution of the affected L5 nerve root, along with positive provocative testing on the affected side. This is pain in a nerve root distribution consistent with the policy's description of a sensory deficit.

**4. Failed conservative therapy**

The plan's policy requires, among other things:

> "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 12 weeks (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This is well beyond the four-week minimum.

> "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

I used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, which is well beyond the three-week minimum.

> "2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

The policy also lists:

> "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification;"

My records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes because of this condition. I am asking my surgeon's office to confirm and, if needed, document any specific activity modification recommendations that were part of my treatment plan, since this detail is not clearly spelled out in the summary I have [surgeon/clinic to confirm and supplement documentation of activity modification, if applicable].

Taken together, my diagnosis, imaging findings, radicular symptoms, and 24 months of progressive, unrelieved pain, along with a full course of physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and an epidural steroid injection that gave only partial relief, show that I have tried and exhausted the conservative measures the plan's own policy describes, and that my condition meets the plan's criteria for this surgery.

## What I Am Asking

I am asking Ambetter to reconsider this denial and approve the requested lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030), based on the medical necessity criteria in your own Clinical Policy CP.MP.114 and the records described above.

I understand that my appeal must be received by **2027-02-19** (my denial notice states 180 days from the date of the notice, 2026-08-23). I am submitting this appeal using the address printed on my denial notice, and I understand I can also find state-specific appeal forms at ambetterhealth.com by selecting my state, or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Reyes's office to complete this review.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Foster**
Member ID: W162894592
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of signature]

Enclosures: [MRI report dated 2026-06-26; physical therapy discharge note; documentation of NSAID use and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-06-17; any additional records provided by Dr. Reyes]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
